mainTopic: Dowry amounts and the wife's perfume fund in the כתובה, and the story of נקדימון בן גוריון's daughter
overview: This amud opens with the last line of an earlier משנה: for dowry goods, the groom writes one-fifth less than their appraised value. A ברייתא then teaches that a father's promised gift to a son-in-law does not pass to the brother who takes his place through יבום, even if that brother is a greater תלמיד חכם. The גמרא explains that the משנה's appraisal examples are not repeats, because each one adds a new point. A new משנה teaches that a cash dowry is written at one and a half times its value, and that the groom adds ten דינרים per מנה for her fund. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it all follows local custom. רב אשי explains that the fund is for perfumes and applies only in ירושלים. His questions about how to count it and how often to pay it end in תיקו. The גמרא then tells of נקדימון בן גוריון's daughter, who once had a huge perfume allowance and was later found starving by רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. Finally, the גמרא begins asking whether נקדימון really failed to give צדקה, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The groom writes one-fifth less
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the earlier משנה: whatever amount the groom writes for her dowry goods is one-fifth less than the value she brings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whatever the groom pledges in the כתובה for her goods, he pledges one-fifth less than their value.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the earlier משנה. It gives a general rule for how the groom records appraised dowry goods in the כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When dowry goods are appraised, the appraisal runs high. So the groom writes an amount one-fifth less than the value she brings. For example, if she brings goods worth 125, he writes 100.

keyTerms.meaning: Pledges or commits to an amount in writing

phrases.english: [whatever] the groom pledges —
he pledges one-fifth less.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶּׁחָתָן פּוֹסֵק הוּא פּוֹסֵק פָּחוֹת חוֹמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous משנה, which began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The amount the groom writes for appraised dowry goods is one-fifth less than their real value.

steps.title: The father-in-law's promise does not pass to the brother
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a father who promised money to his son-in-law can refuse to give it to the dead son-in-law's brother, even if that brother is a תלמיד חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: It goes without saying that this applies when the first husband was a תלמיד חכם and the second is an עם הארץ. But even if the first was an עם הארץ and the second is a תלמיד חכם, the father can say: 'I wanted to give to your brother. To you I do not want to give.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה and brings a ברייתא. It expands on the rule that a father who promised money to his son-in-law does not have to give it to the brother who does יבום after the son-in-law dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the father can refuse only when the brother is a step down, an עם הארץ replacing a תלמיד חכם. The ברייתא says he can refuse even when the brother is an upgrade. The promise was made to one specific person, so it does not pass to anyone else.
steps.confusionAlert: 'First' and 'second' here are two brothers. The first husband died, and the second is his brother who marries her through יבום. They are not two different daughters' husbands.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a promised gift is tied to the person it was promised to, not to whoever fills his place.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
It goes without saying
[when] the first is a Torah scholar
phrases.notes: The 'first' is the son-in-law who died, and the 'second' is his brother who does יבום.

phrases.english: and the second is an unlearned person,
but even if the first is an unlearned person
and the second is a Torah scholar,
he [the father] can say:
'To your brother I wanted to give,
to you I do not want to give.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן אֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא, expanding an earlier ruling of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father's promise of money to a son-in-law does not pass to the brother who does יבום, even if the brother is more learned.

steps.title: Isn't this the same as the first clause?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a thousand דינר and asks why the later cases are taught when they seem to repeat the opening clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'She pledged to bring him a thousand דינר' and so on. But this is the same as the first clause!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about appraisals and complains that the later examples seem to say the same thing as the earlier clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is not supposed to say the same thing twice. If the first clause already taught the rule about appraisals, the extra examples look unnecessary. The challenge pushes us to find what new point each example teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the same as the first clause

phrases.english: She pledged to bring him
a thousand דינר, etc.
This is the same as the first clause!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the ברייתא to a question about how the משנה is worded
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: They seem to repeat the rule already taught in the first clause, and a משנה should not repeat itself.

steps.title: Big and small appraisals, his side and her side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה teaches both a large and a small appraisal, and both the groom's side and the bride's side of the calculation.
steps.simpleTranslation: It taught a large appraisal, and it also teaches a small appraisal. It taught his appraisal, and it also teaches her appraisal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the examples are not true repeats. Each one adds a different angle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the משנה shows the rule works the same for a big dowry (a thousand) and a small one (a hundred). Second, one example looks at what the groom writes, and the other looks at what the bride must bring to match that written amount. So nothing is wasted.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's examples are not repeats. They show the rule applies to large and small amounts, and from both the groom's side and the bride's side.

phrases.english: It taught a large appraisal
and it also teaches a small appraisal.
It taught his appraisal,
phrases.notes: 'His appraisal': he sets the amount, and she must bring enough goods to match it. 'Her appraisal': her goods are valued, and he writes the matching amount.

phrases.english: and it also teaches her appraisal.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא שׁוּמָא רַבָּה וְקָתָנֵי שׁוּמָא זוּטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each clause teaches a distinct point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The later examples seemed to be a plain repeat of the first clause.
steps.terutzMaskana: They add new points: the rule holds for large and small amounts, and the calculation works from both his side and hers.

steps.title: A cash dowry is written at one and a half times its value
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if she brings cash, each סלע is recorded as six דינרים. The groom also adds ten דינרים per מנה for her personal needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she pledged to bring him money, her סלע becomes six דינרים. The groom takes on himself ten דינרים for her fund for every מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains how a dowry of cash, as opposed to goods, is recorded in the כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סלע is four דינרים, but the groom writes six. That adds half, because he can do business with cash and profit from it. He also commits ten דינרים for every hundred she brings, to go toward her personal needs.

keyTerms.meaning: A fund for her personal needs

steps.confusionAlert: Goods are written for less than their value, but cash is written for more. Do not mix up the two rules.

phrases.english: MISHNA: [If] she pledged to bring him money —
her סלע becomes six דינרים.
phrases.notes: A סלע is normally four דינרים, so he writes it as half again more.

phrases.english: The groom takes upon himself
ten דינרים for the fund
for each and every מנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּסְקָה לְהַכְנִיס לוֹ כְּסָפִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new case: a cash dowry instead of goods
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cash dowry is recorded at one and a half times its value, and the groom adds ten דינרים per מנה for her needs.

steps.title: Everything follows local custom
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says these amounts are not fixed. Everything goes by the custom of the place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Everything follows the custom of the region.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with the fixed numbers just given and says local custom decides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion set exact amounts: six דינרים per סלע and ten per מנה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says each place should follow its own practice for these financial terms.
steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion gives fixed amounts for a cash dowry. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says local custom decides.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Everything follows the custom of the region.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר הַכֹּל כְּמִנְהַג הַמְּדִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting opinion within the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The financial terms of a dowry follow local custom rather than fixed amounts.

steps.title: Isn't this the same as the thousand-dinar case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה says a סלע becomes six דינרים, since the earlier משנה already taught that a thousand דינר becomes fifteen מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: This is the same as 'he pledges against them fifteen מנה'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging the new משנה for repeating a rule we already know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סלע is four דינרים, and writing it as six means adding half. The earlier משנה already showed the same thing: a thousand דינר is written as fifteen hundred. So the גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say it twice.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the same as (used to point out a repeat)
He commits to write against them (in the כתובה)
A unit of one hundred דינרים

phrases.english: GEMARA: This is the same as
'he pledges against them fifteen מנה'!
phrases.notes: This quotes the earlier משנה: she brings a thousand דינר, and he writes fifteen hundred. That is the same 'add half' as a סלע becoming six.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ פּוֹסֵק כְּנֶגְדָּם חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר מָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the new משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that each סלע is written as six דינרים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It seems to repeat the earlier rule that a thousand דינר becomes fifteen מנה, which is the same 'add half'.

steps.title: Both a big sum and a small sum are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that one case is a large business sum and one is a small sum, and we could not learn one from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught a large business and he taught a small business. And both are needed. If he had taught only the large business, I would say: that has a lot of profit, so he adds half, but a small business has little profit, so maybe not. And if he had taught only the small business, I would say: that has little expense, but a large business has a lot of expense, so maybe not. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing that each case teaches something the other one could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A big sum makes a lot of profit, so we might think only a big sum earns the extra half. A small sum costs little to manage, so we might think only a small sum earns the extra half. Teaching both shows the husband adds half no matter the size.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is needed (both cases are necessary)
Expense, the cost of managing the money

steps.whatToRemember: The husband adds half to her cash, whether the sum is big or small.

phrases.english: He taught a large business sum,
phrases.notes: The large sum is the thousand דינר from the earlier משנה. The small sum is the single סלע here.

phrases.english: and he taught a small business sum.
And both are needed,
because if he had taught only the large business sum,
which makes a lot of profit,
but a small business sum,
which makes little profit,
I would say no. So it is needed.
phrases.notes: 'No' means: maybe he would not have to add half.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only the small business sum,
which has little expense,
but a large business sum,
which has a lot of expense,
I would say no. So it is needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא עִסְקָא רַבָּה, וּתְנָא עִסְקָא זוּטָא. וּצְרִיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: both cases are needed, because each one teaches something the other could not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From one case alone, we might think the extra half applies only to big sums (more profit) or only to small sums (less expense).
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband adds half for both big and small sums.

steps.title: What is the 'קופה'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ten דינרים 'לקופה' and asks what this fund is.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The groom takes upon himself ten דינר for the קופה.' What is this קופה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה and asks what one word means. This sets up רב אשי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the groom adds ten דינרים per מנה for the 'קופה' but did not say what the fund is for. The גמרא wants to know what it pays for.

keyTerms.meaning: A box or fund set aside for a purpose

phrases.english: 'The groom takes upon himself'
'ten דינר for the fund.'
phrases.notes: This is from the משנה in step 5: ten דינרים for every מנה she brings.

phrases.english: What is this fund?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קוּפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the second part of the משנה from step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the ten-דינר fund is used for.

steps.title: It is a fund for perfumes
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the קופה is a fund for perfumes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: a fund for perfumes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question: the money is for her perfumes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains the 'personal needs' from step 5 more clearly. The ten דינרים per מנה pay for her perfumes.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
A fund for perfumes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: קוּפָּה שֶׁל בְּשָׂמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The קופה is money for perfumes.

steps.title: This rule was said only for ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי adds that the ten-דינר perfume fund was said only for ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אשי said: These words were said only in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a new statement that limits where this rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ten-דינר fund is not a rule for every place. רב אשי says it was said only for ירושלים, so outside ירושלים this fixed amount does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: These words were said only for
ירושלים, the city where this rule applied

phrases.english: And רב אשי said:
These words were not said
except in ירושלים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לֹא נֶאֶמְרוּ דְּבָרִים הַלָּלוּ אֶלָּא בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the rule just explained in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ten-דינר perfume fund was said only for ירושלים.

steps.title: Count ten from which amount?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks whether the ten per מנה is counted from her appraised dowry or from the smaller amount the husband writes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: Is it ten for each appraised מנה, or for each מנה that is accepted?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks a new question about how to count the ten דינרים. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her goods are appraised at one amount, but the husband writes a smaller amount in the כתובה, one-fifth less. רב אשי asks which number we use to count the ten per מנה.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question (that may stay unanswered)
The amount that is accepted (written in the כתובה)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different numbers here: the appraised value of her goods, and the lower value the husband takes on. The question is only about which one to count from.

phrases.english: רב אשי asked:
Is it for each מנה that is appraised,
or for each מנה that is accepted?
phrases.notes: 'Accepted' is the amount the husband writes in the כתובה, which is one-fifth less than the appraisal.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב אָשֵׁי: בְּמָנֶה הַנִּישּׁוֹם, אוֹ בְּמָנֶה הַמִּתְקַבֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a new question about the ten-דינר fund explained in steps 9-11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ten דינרים per מנה are counted from the appraised value or from the reduced value written in the כתובה.

steps.title: How often is the perfume money given?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי continues his questions. Assuming the ten דינרים are counted per accepted מנה, is it a one-time payment or a repeating one: daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is counted from the accepted hundred: is it given only on the first day, or every day? If every day: only the first week, or every week? If every week: only the first month, or every month? If every month: only the first year, or every year?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks a ladder of follow-up questions about how often the husband must give the perfume money. Each question assumes the answer to the one before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 12 asked how much the payment is. These questions ask how often it is paid. Each rung assumes the 'repeating' side of the previous question and then asks whether the payment repeats over a bigger stretch of time.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say: assume this side of the question, and then ask a further question
The accepted מנה, the amount actually taken into account

phrases.english: If you say: per each hundred that is accepted,

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן, אוֹ כׇּל יוֹם וָיוֹם?
phrases.english: is it given on the first day only, or every single day?

phrases.aramaic: אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר כׇּל יוֹם וָיוֹם:
phrases.english: If you say every single day:

phrases.aramaic: שַׁבָּת רִאשׁוֹנָה, אוֹ כׇּל שַׁבָּת וְשַׁבָּת?
phrases.english: is it only the first week, or every week?
phrases.notes: Here שבת means a week, not just the seventh day.

phrases.aramaic: אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר כׇּל שַׁבָּת וְשַׁבָּת:
phrases.english: If you say every week:

phrases.aramaic: חֹדֶשׁ רִאשׁוֹן, אוֹ כׇּל חֹדֶשׁ וָחֹדֶשׁ?
phrases.english: is it only the first month, or every month?

phrases.aramaic: אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר כׇּל חֹדֶשׁ וָחֹדֶשׁ:
phrases.english: If you say every month:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה, אוֹ כׇּל שָׁנָה וְשָׁנָה?
phrases.english: is it only the first year, or every year?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר מָנֶה הַמִּתְקַבֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds directly on רב אשי's question in step 12, moving from 'how much' to 'how often'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How often the ten-דינר perfume payment must be given: once, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.

steps.title: The questions stay unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends רב אשי's chain of questions with תיקו: no answer is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the questions remain open. It has no answer for how often the perfume money is paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו closes a question without deciding it. Here it covers the whole ladder of questions from step 13. The exact amount and how often it is paid are left undecided.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand. The question remains unresolved.

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's questions about how much and how often the perfume money is paid end with no answer (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the questions of step 13 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both of רב אשי's questions stay undecided: whether the ten per מנה is counted from the appraised or the accepted amount, and how often the perfume payment is given.

steps.title: The huge perfume allowance of נקדימון בן גוריון's daughter
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: the חכמים set 400 gold coins for the perfume fund of נקדימון בן גוריון's daughter, for one day. She responded with a blessing, and they answered אמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: There was a case with the daughter of נקדימון בן גוריון. The חכמים set for her 400 gold coins for her perfume fund for that day. She said to them, 'So may you set for your own daughters,' and they answered after her, 'אמן.'
steps.whatsHappening: Still on the topic of the perfume fund, the גמרא tells a story about a very rich woman who got an enormous perfume allowance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה spoke of a small amount, ten דינרים per מנה. This story shows how large the perfume fund could become in a very wealthy family. It also introduces נקדימון בן גוריון's daughter, who is the subject of the next story.

keyTerms.meaning: They set or fixed an amount

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּבִתּוֹ שֶׁל נַקְדִּימוֹן בֶּן גּוּרְיוֹן
phrases.english: There was an incident with the daughter of Nakdimon ben Guryon

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁפָּסְקוּ לָהּ חֲכָמִים אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת זְהוּבִים
phrases.english: for whom the Sages set four hundred gold coins
for the perfume fund, for that very day.
She said to them: This is how you should set for your own daughters,
and they answered after her: Amen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּבִתּוֹ שֶׁל נַקְדִּימוֹן בֶּן גּוּרְיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the unresolved questions about the perfume fund to a story about an extremely large perfume fund.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a wealthy family, the חכמים set a perfume allowance to match her wealth, here 400 gold coins for one day.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי sees a starving young woman
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, leaving ירושלים with his students, saw a young woman picking barley out of animal dung. When she saw him, she covered herself with her hair and stood before him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: There was a case with רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, who was riding on a donkey and leaving ירושלים, with his students walking behind him. He saw a young woman gathering barley from the dung of Arabs' animals. When she saw him, she wrapped herself in her hair and stood before him.
steps.whatsHappening: Connected to נקדימון בן גוריון's daughter, the גמרא begins a ברייתא story. This first part sets the scene for the conversation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman is so poor that she eats barley taken from animal dung. She also has nothing proper to cover herself with, so she uses her hair. The scene is a sharp contrast to the 400 gold coins per day of the previous step.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: The Sages taught: There was an incident with Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai
who was riding on a donkey
and was leaving Jerusalem,
and his students were walking behind him.
He saw a certain young woman
who was gathering barley
from among the dung of the Arabs' animals.
As soon as she saw him,
she wrapped herself in her hair and stood before him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of נקדימון בן גוריון's daughter with a ברייתא about her later life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The scene: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי meets a desperately poor young woman outside ירושלים.

steps.title: She asks for help and reveals who she is
steps.stepSummary: The woman asks רבן יוחנן בן זכאי to support her. He asks who she is, and she answers that she is the daughter of נקדימון בן גוריון.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him, 'My teacher, support me.' He said to her, 'My daughter, who are you?' She said to him, 'I am the daughter of נקדימון בן גוריון.'
steps.whatsHappening: The conversation begins. The poor woman turns out to be the same rich woman from step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the turning point that connects the two stories. The woman who once received 400 gold coins a day for perfume is now begging for food.

keyTerms.meaning: My daughter, a warm way of addressing her

phrases.english: She said to him: My teacher, support me.
He said to her: My daughter, who are you?

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה לוֹ: בַּת נַקְדִּימוֹן בֶּן גּוּרְיוֹן אֲנִי.
phrases.english: She said to him: I am the daughter of Nakdimon ben Guryon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרָה לוֹ: רַבִּי, פַּרְנְסֵנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story and reveals that the poor woman is נקדימון בן גוריון's daughter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The starving woman is the daughter of נקדימון בן גוריון.

steps.title: Where did all the family's money go?
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי asks where her father's wealth went. She answers with a ירושלים proverb about money needing 'salt'. He then asks about her father-in-law's wealth, and she says the one destroyed the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her, 'My daughter, where did your father's money go?' She said, 'My teacher, isn't this the proverb they say in ירושלים: the salt of money is lacking?' Some say the proverb is: the salt of money is kindness. He asked, 'And where is your father-in-law's money?' She said, 'This one came and destroyed that one.'
steps.whatsHappening: She explains why her family's huge fortune disappeared. Money needs 'salt' to keep it, and her family's wealth was lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proverb compares money to meat, which needs salt to keep from spoiling. One version says the money lacked its salt. The other version says that salt is חסד, kindness. Her father-in-law's money was also lost because it got mixed with her father's.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'salt' of money, what keeps it from being lost

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ: בִּתִּי, מָמוֹן שֶׁל בֵּית אָבִיךָ הֵיכָן הָלַךְ?
phrases.english: He said to her: My daughter, the money of your father's household, where did it go?

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה לוֹ: רַבִּי, לָא כְּדֵין מָתְלִין מַתְלָא בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם:
phrases.english: She said to him: My teacher, isn't this the proverb they tell in Jerusalem:
'The salt of money is lacking'?
phrases.notes: Think of money like meat: without salt to preserve it, it goes bad and is lost.

phrases.english: And some say it: 'kindness.'
And the money of your father-in-law's household, where is it?
phrases.notes: This is רבן יוחנן בן זכאי asking again, even though the text doesn't say so.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה לוֹ: בָּא זֶה וְאִיבֵּד אֶת זֶה.
phrases.english: She said to him: This one came and destroyed that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לַהּ: בִּתִּי, מָמוֹן שֶׁל בֵּית אָבִיךָ הֵיכָן הָלַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the conversation and explains how the family's wealth was lost.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wealth lasts only when it is 'salted', which one version explains as kindness. Her father's money lacked that, and it dragged down her father-in-law's money too.

steps.title: She reminds him of her כתובה, and he recalls its huge sum
steps.stepSummary: The daughter asks רבן יוחנן בן זכאי if he remembers signing her כתובה. He tells his students that he did, and that it listed a million gold דינרים from her father's house, besides what came from her father-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: My teacher, do you remember when you signed my כתובה? He said to his students: I remember signing this woman's כתובה, and I read in it: a million gold דינרים from her father's house, not counting what came from her father-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on: the daughter proves who she is by reminding רבן יוחנן בן זכאי that he was a witness on her כתובה. He confirms it and tells his students how rich she once was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line shows how far she has fallen. The same woman whose כתובה listed a million gold coins is now picking barley out of animal dung. That sharp contrast sets up רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's tears in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Marriage contract, which lists what the bride brings and what she is owed
Signed (here, as a witness on the document)

phrases.english: She said to him: My teacher,
do you remember when you signed on my marriage contract?
He said to his students:

phrases.aramaic: זָכוּר אֲנִי כְּשֶׁחָתַמְתִּי עַל כְּתוּבָּתָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ,
phrases.english: I remember when I signed on the marriage contract of this woman,
and I was reading in it:

phrases.aramaic: אֶלֶף אֲלָפִים דִּינְרֵי זָהָב מִבֵּית אָבִיהָ,
phrases.english: a thousand thousand gold dinars from her father's house,
aside from what came from her father-in-law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרָה לוֹ: רַבִּי, זָכוּר אַתָּה כְּשֶׁחָתַמְתָּ עַל כְּתוּבָּתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the conversation from step 18. She now reminds him of her past wealth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her כתובה once listed a million gold dinars from her father, plus more from her father-in-law.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי cries over the fate of ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי cries and says: when ישראל does רצונו של מקום, no nation rules over them. When they do not, they are handed to a lowly nation, and even to that nation's animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי cried and said: How fortunate you are, ישראל! When they do God's will, no nation or people can rule over them. When they do not do God's will, He hands them over to a lowly nation, and not just to a lowly nation, but even to the animals of a lowly nation.
steps.whatsHappening: Seeing how low she has fallen, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי cries and draws a lesson for all of ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He teaches that ישראל's fate depends on whether they do רצונו של מקום. Doing it brings full freedom, and not doing it brings deep shame. The last line, 'even the animals of a lowly nation,' points straight at this woman, who was looking for food in animal dung.
steps.whatToRemember: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's lesson: ישראל's freedom or shame depends on whether they do רצונו של מקום. This woman's fall is a living example.

phrases.aramaic: בָּכָה רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai cried and said:
How fortunate are you, Israel,
at a time when they do the will of the Omnipresent,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין כׇּל אוּמָּה וְלָשׁוֹן שׁוֹלֶטֶת בָּהֶם,
phrases.english: no nation or tongue rules over them,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִזְמַן שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: and at a time when they do not do the will of the Omnipresent,
He hands them over into the hand of a lowly nation.
And not only into the hand of a lowly nation,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּיַד בְּהֶמְתָּן שֶׁל אוּמָּה שְׁפָלָה.
phrases.english: but even into the hand of the animals of a lowly nation.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּכָה רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי וְאָמַר: אַשְׁרֵיכֶם יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After hearing how rich she used to be, he reacts with tears and a lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When ישראל does רצונו של מקום, no nation rules them. When they do not, they are handed over to a lowly nation, and even to its animals.

steps.title: Did נקדימון really not give charity?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the story's hint that נקדימון בן גוריון did not give צדקה. It begins quoting a ברייתא about the fine woolen garments that were used when he walked to the בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And did נקדימון בן גוריון not give צדקה? But it was taught in a ברייתא: They said about נקדימון בן גוריון that when he would leave his house to go to the בית המדרש, fine woolen garments would be...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops the story to ask a question: the story suggests נקדימון lost his money because he did not give צדקה, but a ברייתא seems to show he was very generous. The quote from the ברייתא starts here and continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her answer in step 18, that money needs 'salt,' meant her father did not give enough צדקה. The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that נקדימון seemed to act with great generosity. That makes the story look like it contradicts another source.
steps.confusionAlert: The story never says outright that נקדימון did not give צדקה. The גמרא is reading that into her saying about money needing 'salt' (step 18), and the question is aimed at that hint.

phrases.aramaic: וְנַקְדִּימוֹן בֶּן גּוּרְיוֹן לָא עֲבַד צְדָקָה?
phrases.english: And did Nakdimon ben Guryon not perform charity?
phrases.notes: Her saying in step 18, that money needs 'salt,' hinted that he lost his wealth for not giving צדקה.

phrases.english: But it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל נַקְדִּימוֹן בֶּן גּוּרְיוֹן
phrases.english: They said about Nakdimon ben Guryon
that when he would leave his home for the study hall,
fine woolen garments would be

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנַקְדִּימוֹן בֶּן גּוּרְיוֹן לָא עֲבַד צְדָקָה? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and questions the hint, from step 18, that נקדימון did not give צדקה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The hint in the story (her 'salt' saying) that נקדימון lost his wealth because he did not give צדקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא describes נקדימון acting with great generosity, so how can the story suggest he did not give צדקה?
